page: Amazon Web Services c8a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. It is powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9R45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs without multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, complemented by support for advanced vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware configurations exclude integrated local disk storage and discrete GPUs, relying on remote network-attached volumes for persistent data and delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the c8a.xlarge demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, achieving 3,773.48 in stress-ng single-core tests and a Geekbench single-core score of 2,760.0. This translates into high compression throughput, reaching 41.5 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 18.32 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. In small LLM execution (135M model), text generation reaches top-tier throughput at 361.71 tokens per second.

Multi-core execution and overall memory subsystem testing show moderate results consistent with a 4-core, 8 GB envelope. Multi-core stress-ng registers at 15,071.65, multi-threaded bzip3 delivers 71.77 GB/sec, and the Geekbench multi-core score settles at 8,805.0. Memory bandwidth achieves 52.9 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 34.45 GB/sec for uncached writes, while the PassMark memory score falls into the lower quartile. This architectural profile provides efficient single-threaded compute density, though workloads are constrained by the 8.0 GB aggregate RAM limit and the absence of local NVMe storage.

Given its high clock speed, strong single-threaded instruction throughput, and balanced 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio, the c8a.xlarge is well tailored for compute-bound batch processing, single-threaded compiling tasks, static web serving (benchmarked at 24.13 GB/sec), and lightweight microservices. The lack of bundled local storage and modest memory capacity make it less suitable for large in-memory databases or data-intensive analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c8a.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9R45 x86_64 processor. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides 4 dedicated physical cores (4 vCPUs) paired with 8.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a 1:2 core-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing network-attached storage and providing a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate top-tier single-threaded performance, with exceptional single-core Geekbench and compression metrics, alongside middle-tier multi-threaded and memory throughput scores. The configuration delivers strong compute efficiency for workloads needing high single-core execution speed within a constrained memory footprint, making it suitable for web serving, microservices, code compilation, and batch processing tasks.
